links.outcome: Patient-perceived understandability of plain-language AI-simplified Arabic reports versus traditional radiologist reports (Likert 1-5)
links.effect: Median 1 (IQR 1-2) for AI-simplified Arabic vs 5 (IQR 3-5) for traditional reports (p<0.001; r=0.97); 94.9% (93/98) preferred the Arabic simplified version.
links.quote: AI-simplified Arabic reports produced a median perceived understandability score of 1 (IQR 1-2) versus 5 (IQR 3-5) for traditional reports (p < 0.001; rank-biserial r = 0.97), with 94.9% (93/98) of patients preferring the Arabic simplified version.

links.outcome: Radiologist-assessed hallucination rate and safety of AI-simplified reports for patient release
links.effect: 96.9% (95/98) of reports safe for patient release; hallucination rate 3.1% (n=3; 1 unsafe, 2 safe by consensus).
links.quote: Safety evaluation demonstrated 96.9% (95/98) of reports safe for patient release, with a hallucination rate of 3.1% (n = 3; 1 unsafe, 2 safe by consensus).

unlisted_practices: On-site, institutionally governed LLM deployment for patient-facing report simplification to preserve data privacy
Fine-tuned dedicated Arabic translation stage in a two-stage simplification pipeline

screen.reason: Prospective feasibility and safety evaluation of an on-site Arabic/English radiology report simplification LLM pipeline with 98 outpatients and 3 board-certified radiologists, assessing understandability and safety.
